thread_title: Jordan’s 2019 Log ( NO OFF TOPIC POSTS)
author: Jordan Peters
content:
Hey chaps, so my pushes up have always been after comps, so lean start points
These were the big pushes to break plateaues. 2008-2012 gaining size was very very easy. I gained 15 pounds stage weight a year just from training hard and eating . It was after that I had to really push to get more
2012 : 210 – 280 , when I came back down in 2013 I was 230 . So I got 20 pounds stage weight in one year there.
2013-2014 I didn’t have much time as I did the back end of 2013 and early 2104 , so I went upto 248 only , then 2014 showing was 237.
After this was the next big push, 240 – 300 , when came down in 2015 was 248
After that went upto 286 , came back down to same kinda weight 246 in 2016 . Didn’t get any new muscle but the look was better.
2017 was a manic year , we did our masters , moved house , and the business really started to show. So I didn’t go up heavy , Max I was 275 I didn’t compete this year .
2018 I went up over 300 , then came down to 248.  I stayed very tight after this to try to fix my waist , Max I went was 260 . This totally backfired as I didn’t regain all my size so 2019 I didn’t compete, I was down at 240 and still not ready . Then after that it’s been 240-280 , then mini cut to 265 , then push to 292 and then I’m on the way down now 🙂
As you can see each push up yields less and less , but in total it’s been 100 pounds of Stage weight added since I started.

content:
Curt it’s not silly , I’m actually
Happy , as most people think the opposite , and want to do more and more sets to failure . Now you could potentially just leave it there , your right , but I would say it depends on your frequency your training at. 1 set does yield a lot of stimulus , but at some point you need more ( not much , but defo some) . So let’s say after a year of full body work , doing just 1 set every other day, you then move to upper lower , this is where 2 sets would be more beneficial and a necessity because you have more muscle and because you can’t make big adaptive responses from just one set. Why do I go lighter ? – potentiation , basically . Heavy weights then make light weights feel REALLY light , so after a 5-9 , a 10-15 I can then use a little more load than if I did it fresh , because my muscles are so primed to work. Hope that helps

content: I will share this convo with myself and Corinne today after her session. She hit an all time 8 rep pb pause squat – 160kg , unreal set as it was a true 2 count . I set the numbers , the sessions, and dictate when we go up and down with Corinne’s lifts , if I push her too fast her back tells us to fuck off . thread_title: Jordan’s 2019 Log ( NO OFF TOPIC POSTS)
author: Jordan Peters
content:
I will add , exercise order is about being able to lift the most amount of weight on the exercises across the session.
So – preciously I did adductor last because I thought it would take away from my compound lifts . It doesn’t , it actually helps as it gets my knees warmer .
Your sessions want to be ordered in a way that allows for the absolute largest load in each movement . So does that mean doing leg ext before the compound stuff , probably yes , if volume is low . As means you can get higher loading on that and not take away from the compound work.
This is obv all person dependant , if you do adductor and ham first like me and ur compound work dies, order it in an appropriate way
There are some exercises I won’t ever do in the later stages of a session because of their strength curve , a fatigued muscle can’t perform well against those movements , so they go earlier – most hammer strength kit

thread_title: Eq or npp to start off contest prep?
author: Jordan Peters
content:
Tren goes in when performance potentially drops , start low, add more as needed .
You can start no probs with nandrolone but it has to come out at some point , and u will need to replace that dose with test or eq to replicate fullness . Defo not a problem to Do, I do it, but it’s easier to just start without imo . I have just set Jamie’s start cycle for prep at 500
Test , 600 eq, 1g primo, 100 Anavar / day.
We will drop the primo for some tren at some point and have a break from the orals , test and eq will go up based on what he can handle to balance detail : fullness.

author: Jordan Peters
content:
So my view point is this, once u have decided it’s trt time, which every needs to at some point , mine will be 150mg/week , that will be legit trt . I will then just let my body do whatever it does on that dose , I will train as hard as I can and see how much I can fight the process , the process will take me down to probably 210-230 after a year depending on how fat I am . Then I have my baseline,
Then it starts again – progressive overload at just that recovery capability , strength . U can still progress lifts! It’s just going to be much less weight than before . So let’s say my incline barbell pb is 4 plates x 10 , once trt has done its thing I imagine my absolute best would be 2 and half plates for 10 , maybe 130 max. Then the goal is get that to 140. So the session is still you versus you, just in that moment of time.

thread_title: Jordan’s 2019 Log ( NO OFF TOPIC POSTS)
author: Jordan Peters
content: The soft music is much better fuel for me. Take Hans zimmer – time for example . Everyone reading this now, get that up on your phone and start the song at 2 mins, put headphones in turn them up as loud as u can. Now imagine what you want in your life , what you want from competing, what you want to achieve…. now think about times when u didn’t get what you wanted , when you really felt pain , like real pain – like for me , I think about nearly losing Corinne – the only thing in my life that really makes any sense. I think about growing up without a mum and why that happened – I think about the pain I went through when I had therapy for 6 months , when I was laying on my kitchen floor having panic attack’s that I couldn’t even get up . I relive those moments and then picture all those things standing between me and the set , in that moment the only way to win those battles in my head is to win the set. Keep focusing on the music and just absolutely unleash every bit of emotional power you have . At 2 mins 35 that song starts to drop.at 3 mins 5 is when I would start my set for example and if im really fresh – by that point I’m absolutely in a diff place

thread_title: Jordan’s 2019 Log ( NO OFF TOPIC POSTS)
author: Jordan Peters
content:
Re knee pain, so chaps my approach with bpc and tb500
Is solely for accuse injuries. Relying on those for tendon issues, isn’t smart! Reason being, tendon inflammation is solely down to exercise selection and execution. You can get that pain out real fast if your smart ! So I strongly advise fixing the root cause. Acutr injuries are diff, you didn’t see those coming and they are just part and parcel, so small fibre tears , which happen for me usually once a month , in some body part , pec a lot, quad a lot, I use those. If knees and elbows flare , I change my exercises – use curcumin, Boswellia ( join in ) and I’m ready to rock.
Kwang loong use pre/during wo. Dit da jow 3-4 times a day. I won’t even need them as the last session altering my order of exercises and dropping leg extension I have most of the knee pain gone already. Always always address the cause, don’t just mask it

thread_title: Jordan’s 2019 Log ( NO OFF TOPIC POSTS)
author: Jordan Peters
content:
Very good! There is merit to the rir approach, but something about it is off , not doing those final reps can’t be made up for by extra volume imo – I thought it could but the weights I am now touching are back In line with usual rate of progression for me. I can’t prove it, but I can feel it , in regards to the effective reps idea. There needs to be a lot more looking at what reps 2/1/0 rir do. I think that training for it in phases could be useful , to increase then the effectiveness of taking sets all the way there. I absolutely don’t agree that volume needs to drive up quickly . One thing I heard Mike say that I absolutely disagree with, is that we will stop responding to the same volume very quickly – now I have used the same volume for years , so has James, so has Corinne, so has Mark , so has Oscar, so has Joe – I can go on and on here and all of us have built WAY more muscle than any one that supports the idea of needing to increase volume at rapid rates. That I would say is the only thing I strongly disagree with , and the reason for it- you won’t get maximally strong , and does that change looks more than anything else, without a doubt yes. Name 3 of the most muscular uk bodybuilders – James, Luke , Nathan – all 3 , are outrageously strong . All 3 don’t drive their volume up rapidly , they focus on driving their strength. I love looking into systems to learn more, and although I only ran it 8 weeks, in that time I wasn’t close To lifting my usual weights , plain and simply – no amount of volume , at intensity off failure , using sub max weights , will
Build more muscle .

thread_title: Jordan’s 2019 Log ( NO OFF TOPIC POSTS)
author: Jordan Peters
content: Dan, totally fair question , but let’s look at it properly . Steps are an energy balance requirement , to create a deficit . We have the following tools : diet, cardio, fat burners, steps, training volume. If someone has a really active job , have great resilience to metabolic adaptation, are taking lots of fat burners – they may need zero additional steps! Or .. someone the total opposite may need 3000 , or 5000 , or 10,000 or some bikini girls 15-20,000!! Each of the above tool influences the other , so how many steps do I shoot for? – the total needed in that moment to create a deficit without causing too much leg fatigue

author: Jordan Peters
content:
So my thought process with the split :
What’s the number of days I can train in a row before I need a rest .
What’s the number of sets I can do in a sesssion and recover for the next time I hit than body part
Am I selecting exercises that target my weaknesses as a priority
Am I selecting exercises that allow for optimal loading and progression

author: Jordan Peters
content:
I’m a huge Ryan Terry fan, works so hard and a lovely guy.
So remember these guys are coaches , they often will recount their way of training . We also must remember they are at the Olympia , so that shows you they have some incredible genetics when combined with their hard work. SO as mentioned above they will grow on any split.
At some point as I talk about a split routine is needed but I feel we will all take a big step forward by training upper / lower or full body splits

author: Jordan Peters
content:
So I don’t believe in a best training programme , as it’s so auto regulated ( you adjust based on your needs / reactions, I.e volume /
Frequency )
But I do think a lot of people will benefit from an upper lower split and just focusing on getting very strong

thread_title: Jordan’s 2018 Log ( NO OFF TOPIC POSTS)
author: Jordan Peters
content:
Paul defo yes, That will never change . Remember training is just about creating adaptations , so the underlying base is there and then after periods of time you feel out nuances that will apply to you the individual.
My underlying thoughts on training are unchanged for a v long time now :
Beginners – full body , train as frequent as poss, only do the hard stuff . Zero fluff
Intermediate – upper lower , little more focus on weaker areas but still focus on the hard stuff
Advanced , push pull legs , add in more iso work, focus on stuff that struggles to grow
Pro level , split stuff up even more to focus even more on stuff that needs extra focus
That is how I take clients from start to
Finish: I have clients that have had for 5 years now and added 20kg stage weight to; and this is the general process we went through

author: Jordan Peters
content:
So my take on carb powders guys and this is something Dr Scott Stevenson taught me back in 2012 and it still stands true.
During off season, we are typically overloaded with cals , digestion isn’t as efficient , and gastric emptying is usually slower. In this instance, using a really efficient carb powder that has a lower molecular weight, is advantageous as it will sit better during training.
During prep, if you are still using some intra carbs, you can likely get away with any powder at all here. As your likely to be hungrier, gastric emptying is fast , so the likelyhood of bloat is far diminished .
Cluster bomb by redcon COMBINED with breach, as we need electrolytes to most efficiently utilise those carbs intra. All of the literature showing fast gut clearance uses electrolytes.

thread_title: does growth suppress your natural gh

content: In the moment that it is active , it will impact yes but there is no negative feedback loop in the same manner as test or thyroid, in that you won’t shut down gh production. author: Jordan Peters
content:
Jesse, the idea of metabolic damage is an interesting one and it isn’t something that’s supported in the literature as being a long term thing . Sure we have a decline in metabolic rate when we diet , but this is often related a lot to a decreases in body weight resulting in a decrease in energy expenditure therefore bmr decreases. This is immediately fixed once u regain weight . Equally the decline in leptin and hormonal issues are normalised once you are back to normal weight .
SO if you can’t handle many calories this is always relative to your energy expenditure , I would look at your neat levels, your daily steps and your volume / effort in sessions. And look to increase all of those things
I do always advise a mini cut if body fat is too high to keep gaining muscle effectively , regardless of your caloric intake

author: Jordan Peters
content:
Ben is setting a volume that is like q fail safe. He isn’t to know how intense ppl train, and volume we know is usually a driver of hypertrophy ( unless u train like an absolute crazy person / ala Dorian) . So Ben has been smart there and thought well if I give them 8 sets , some growing has to occur and then if I give them 5 drops , some metabolite accumulation has to occur.
I have never needed as much volume because A I train at higher frequency, so Beating the living shit out of a muscle will limit that and B I can cause a ton of muscle damage because I’m strong .
Feel out your volume , see how you recover from the prescribed volume and adjust accordingly . It’s never about what you can do but what you can recover from

author: Jordan Peters
content: Austin, it depends is the answer. I think we can all be mindful of ensuring we are loading muscles. You will see on a lot of my videos that will be Coming up that for now, as I focus on really engaging the muscle that I will almost pause at the fully lengthened position under load, to be totally accurate as to what initiates the movement . Once I have drummed in this level of internal cueing , I can make that more of a single movement as opposed to a pause which would take my loading down a fair bit. The exercises you select is up to you. If you like barbell press, then banding it is maybe wise , but equally so using dumbells offers a really Gd profile as an exercise anyways , the humerus come to the midline of the body so shortening the muscle is easier than on a barbell ( hence the use of bands to over load the top end to force a greater contraction where the contraction would normally drop off)

author: Jordan Peters
content:
Cluster sets like muscle rounds really do allow people to reach failure in a way that is often better form,
As the first few sets are totally sub max,
So the focus can literally just totally be on execution. And then hopefully that perfect execution carries through to the set where you reach failure ( often it doesn’t and this set goes to shit with ppl form wise)
But with a muscle round try to make the first 4 reps just immaculate as the load is light and then attempt to replicate that form all the way to failure

author: Jordan Peters
content:
pedro, these are awesome question, but hard to answer , so il do my best to explain my thoughts.
I do spill a little still, just into the areas still holding fat. your body wont ever adjust to this if still holding fat, you will just spill less once leaner. once truly lean, its then v hard to spill, especially when lowering water. when I carb up this time I will reduce my water intake. yday on 1280 carb I drank maybe 8 litres of water, if I drank only 3, I probably wont of spilled much at all. once I am ready, my first day of carbs will likely be 1200g on 3 litres and I wont spill whatso ever
I don’t believe pepto pro is more effective. that’s speculation. I feel it will stimulate MPS just like any other protein, so I max out any MPS potential at every feed, regardless of the source of protein.
SO, where my food is there, has evolved from offseason. when I reduce cals, I pull food from where I feel I need it least. I’m never hungry at breakfast and I don’t care for carbs there, so I personally am happy with a small breakfast. pre workout meal also I’m happy for it to be small, I don’t like training on a full stomach. some people like big carb meals for breakfast and pre gym, if that’s the case that is fine. I’m just not one of those
post workout I like a big meal, our body can utilise carbs best here, so it makes sense for this to be the highest intake of the day. the meal after equally I like to be a bit higher than pre wo usually. IF I still needed to be on more carbs, I would still have some pre bed. but as my food lowers, I would rather keep my food a little higher around the workout so I pull the carbs and or fats pre bed. in offseason I usdually end up needing carbs here , I was having yoghurt berries and almond butter which was totalling about 35 carb and 30 fat.
once my comp is fin I will work back in my carbs and they will likely end up being every meal as I foresee my metabolism increasing a lot post show

author: Jordan Peters
content: so I was asked today, how come u never really moan about being tired, or lethargic, or beat up. And its an interesting question, but tbh how does expressing those feelings help in anyway? I think this is defo an experience thing and I get that it comes with time, but I think making it your goal to not even entertain those thoughts/ideas, is a gd thing. in the prep I did with Milos, when I legit had panic attacks in the push up, and on the way down after dropping 60 pounds and collapsing before stage, I didn’t tell him once that I was tired, or hungry or weak…. that info isn’t useful to him at all. inside I was dying, so much so I was in tears at a week out from true exhaustion, but I didn’t even consider letting him know that, why would I want to tell him that I was mentally weak. do you think the winner would show that weakness…. or even a version of ones self that truly wanted to achieve a new goal or milestone, would or should entertain that kind of mental weakness.

jdh, Marcus…. the goal of comp prep is the least amount of body fat possible. there is no such thing as low food, when that is the goal. that is ALL that matters, yes they do all those things function wise, but when onstage…are you going to hold your hand up and say, well I’m 7 pounds off because I didn’t want to pull my calories too low because I wanted to maintain the function of fats…while the dude that is peeled out of his mind laughs at you haha. remember, everything is in context. this isn’t maintainable, healthy, steady dieting. this is comp prep 🙂 , fats can go right back in when prep is done. right now I couldn’t give a fuck about the role of fats for inflammation and health, I care about glycogen , muscle fullness, and how hard I can train 🙂

author: Jordan Peters
content:
Adam, gd question. This is usually going to be a trial and error set up for most.
So let’s say you do legs twice a week ( my general advise for everyone is to do that)
Let’s say heavy quads , light hams – you go in at 6 sets for quads , 4 sets for hams. Maybe a couple sets of direct glute work. Some adductor work- usually like a rest pause set and 3-4 sets of calves. The next session is just a flip side , 6 ham ( including a deadlift variation) , 4 quad. A couple glute , then adductor work again. Rotate exercises, and progress lifts. After 5-6 weeks you should be able to tell if the set totals are right , as you should still be making gd progress with your lifts. If stuff is stalling , you then cut back a set from each session. And then see how that impacts recovery

author: Jordan Peters
content: Holding off Using insulin in the post show window shouldn’t actually be about insulin sensitivity IMO, we are using insulin to hugely increase protein synthesis and offset muscle protein breakdown. So waiting , makes little sense if the goal is to use it at some stage; the leaner you are , the more efficient it will be at aiding muscle growth , provided you are back to training REALLY hard ASAP . Also using mega low doses again doesn’t make sense, how are we going to maximise it’s protein synthetic effects. It seems people are thinking solely about glycogen storage, which of course does play a role in muscle building via increase in cellular hydration – more water in the cell due to increased glycogen equals more muscle BUT protein synthesis increase is what will really build muscle. Therefore 5-6iu is a great dose , ensure your diet is set up appropriately

thread_title: Intra Workout Carbs: why is it beneficial?
author: Jordan Peters
content:
ok, I don’t feel intra wo supps are a MUST. but I feel they do pose some benefit. the intake of carbs here wont offset gh release, that isn’t accuratr physiology. the intra wo carbs here will also help control cortisol from becoming too high, which may then force the body to mobilise proteins for fuel, if at that moment we are in net muscle protein breakdown, we potentially could breakdown muscle and convert those aminos to glycogen via gluconeogenesis. so by having readily available carbs and aminos, we avoid this.
amounts needed would be reflective of your carb allowance/day. id say putting 20percent of your total daily carb allowance intra poses some gd benefit

author: Jordan Peters
content:
zero cardio, I shall copy and paste in my post on this from previous
My stance on offseason cardio:
I get asked this a lot so I will breakdown my opinion.
If your offseason goal is to build muscle, you need a caloric surplus to achieve this. You can’t grow in a deficit ( unless using a gd wack of drugs, but let’s assume we are natural/ cruising on an amount that replaces natural levels).
Typically you will need a 200-300 cal surplus a day to create new tissue, so each week total calories need to go up to ensure we stay in a surplus.
If we perform cardio, we then take away from some of that surplus ( energy in/ energy out) and if we want to build muscle , we then simply have to eat more again. During a phase in which we are trying to maximise strength, particularly leg strength , this makes no sense. Cardio is going to hinder our recovery capabilities. Therefore resting and doing no cardio and simply eating a little less to keep body fat in check ( but still remain in a surplus ) makes much more sense.
What if you find without cardio your training performance suffers? This is common in heavy bodybuilders, I experience this a lot in offseason that once I’m over 280 pounds, my ability to work hard in the sessions suffers. So could cardio here be an option. In most cases I would still say no, as admittedly I was just too heavy and should of been carrying 10 pounds less crap weight, to maximise training performance.
Your training should place demands on your fitness, if it doesn’t, tailor your rest periods in some parts to achieve that goal , challenge your heart rate and this will see fitness improve.
Save your cardio as a tool for when your looking to expend energy and push further into a deficit. That is the role of cardio from a body composition perspective ( do more, burn more cals, push to a deeper deficit and drop fat ) and even then use this as sparingly as possible , like any of the other tools at your disposal to creating a caloric deficit ( food drops, fat burners, increasing training volume )
JP

content:
hey toby,
I see nothing wrong with big meals like that, your net energy balance is what underpins fat loss/gain. so you tell me?…are the scales going up So fast that your becoming horribly fat, or is your current food holding you steady weight wise. I used to eat like you when I was at my first uni, I did a lot of salmon and rice and beef and pasta, the combos of meals never made a diff, only total cals. I dropped weight if missed meals, and got fat if I added in cheesy chips ontop of my daily meals as that then pushed me over my caloric needs.
re natural limits, I feel any which way you approach it you will end roughly with the same muscle when dieted back down. staying leaner means you don’t have to over diet, getting fatter means harsher dieting and compromising muscle. so once at your genetic ceiling, there isn’t much you can do beyond being stubborn with your progressive loading and eating to an amount that ensures you are happy with body fat levels.

author: Jordan Peters
content:
fats slow absortion of carbs in the g.i and they lessen the insulin response from the food. we want to totally maximise this period, so using donuts cookies etc is a poor choice plus your caloric intake will just sky rocket way beyond what you need on a daily basis to grow and it would be impossible to stay in a caloric deficit unless you have 1 mini donut and 1 small cookie LOL.
I also feel just taking in carbs pwo isn’t as useful as pre intra post, we need readily available fuel to optimise training. we also have greater glycogen uptake abiity intra due to higher glut 4 elevation and high enzyme activity (glycogen synthase) , therefore if your daily carb allowance is 250, id likely have 40-50 pre wo meal, 50-60g intra and the rest as a pwo meal.

author: Jordan Peters
content:
264, hit the target I wanted for the week without a dietary change and tbh I think I can go again next week without one, the run of progressions in training and looking to keep moving faster and training harder , is creating a huge caloric output. I haven’t ever done full body workouts as hard as this, and can attest the fat burning potential is pretty crazy. its taking a lot of mental focus to ensure every session is where it needs to be, but I’m making it happen still.
I made a fb post the other day that covered my thoughts on really ensuring your training is V V hard, I simply don’t see unless you have ridiculous amounts of muscle why you need things like arm days and shoulder days as the energy output in them is a joke ( remember pros are pros for a reason, they will be pros training however they want, they are the genetic elite, so following what pros do, makes no sense, unless of course you are also the genetic elite and can look great doing just arm days that burn no cals) , and then if you do hammer your body with volume in an arm session to create an energy output, you then cant train that body part with any frequency to make the most of protein synthesis in the muscle returning to baseline in 24 hours plus you likely then write off your pressing ability from all the super beneficial tricep pushdowns that have been done LOL.
I have always favoured upper lower splits and push pull leg splits for this reason, but what I haven’t done previously is pushed the volume a little higher for each body part to ensure total session volume is high enough to bring about a really really hard session. so previously lets say I would do 4 sets for back in an upper lower split, now il push that to 7 or 8. same for chest , delts, tris. you need to vary the rep ranges and intensity approaches to each exercise so as to not over reach neurally by just going heavy heavy heavy, all the time. you need to push the volume to a point that the total work in a session is the limit you can handle before you cant recover efficiently to string together 3-5 weeks of training. if you burn out in 2, that’s not ideal, but If you can get 3 weeks of horrible work in then need to deload for a week, that to me is acceptable. just imagine how hard you would have to train ,to over reach in 3 weeks, those sessions would be so fucked up and nasty, but then think of how that would change your body. this is how you need to look at this, if you want changes fast

author: Jordan Peters
content:
I will add. It seems that the most influential factor on hyper trophy, is using the maximum amount of weight you can use, for the maximum amount of volume you can recover from.
SO let’s think how that would transpire into a training set up.
We can’t sustain a high enough total volume from really heavy loading, eg 3 reps per set. We would need to do 10 work sets to acquire enough volume to force an adaptation – that’s not realistic. However a load that we can do for 10 reps for 3 sets is heavy enough to recruit a large amount of muscle fibres and we can neurally recover from 3 sets. Some people will be able to efficiently do sets of 6-8 and be able to do 4 sets to acquire enough total volume to grow. However others it will see them burnout quite quickly. So it’s a safe bet that a weight you can handle for 8-12 reps, is typically the most efficient for hypertrophy.

author: Jordan Peters
content:
Just to add to corinnes post.
Like she mentioned we are using the shake essentially as an extra meal. Pre workout meal is 90mins-2 hours pre workout. This then means there is potential to fully maximise protein synthesis across the workout , as we can do this every 2-3 hours. Therefore it makes sense to use the same amount of protein at least , which you have in a normal meal. I say at least as there is even greater potential around the workout to further increase protein synthesis due to anabolic signalling from liftin weights, so you can use an extra 20-30g of protein here if you wish and your body can utilise it. Using 40g from a complete protein is the most efficient way. Then using more performance based aminos ontop like creatine and beta alanine

joe, they aren’t a must at all. if calories are low and you like eating, eat your carbs pre and post workout. if calories are high, and you have say 50-100g carbs that you could happily not consume as food, shift this to intra workout. I don’t feel intra workout is a huge must, it can help recovery potentially, but it isn’t a must.
I always use intra wo in offseason and as I get closer to shows that’s what comes out as cals drop.
what is important, when using intra is to use good quality ingredients. a complete protein will elevate muscle protein synthesis to the greatest extent and offset muscle protein breakdown to the greatest extent. so I advise pepto pro , you need around 20g protein minimum to bring about optimal muscle protein synthesis, this can be elevated further by adding 2-3g of leucine ( leucine content is what further underpins the process) . using an efficient carb powder in sync that will help the whole process ( protein + carb, raises insulin levels more so , which is ideal at this time frame) I like cyclic dextrins, as they are easily digested and cause steady blood sugar levels, when sipping across a session

hey buddy,
ok I would reduce work sets to 2 max per exercise initially, and attack those two sets. this makes lift progressions more efficient. separate the rep ranges too. 5-9, 10-15. this will get you much stronger much faster.
don’t lower back load on consecutive days in the same heavy rep range, leg press is ideal here

everything else looks gd exercise choice wise

I like single leg presses, just ensure your eccentric control is good
I like to leg press deep, I bottom out machines normally, this is how I have always leg pressed, sure if lower back is coming off a lot, its not wise, but docking depth is just going to result in insufficient muscle recruitment
I don’t wear a belt ever, that’s what spinal erectors are for 🙂

so as a prep continues you have less food, and doing more cardio, so there is constant risk of dropping tissue, so lets say every 2 weeks you add 10 percent of your total mg/week to your cycle, your going to protect things a lot more. I prefer cruising before I start a prep so then I can start low dose wise, so then 10percnt is only ever like 180mg or so.
most of my clients I feel going back in at 750-1000mg total a week , following a cruise, is a gd start point for a prep, it depends how easily they build muscle, how long they have had fresh muscle ( this is harder to keep) . so that would look like 500mg test, 500mg equipoise again as an example. then after two weeks could add 100mg dbol across the week. then couple weeks later add 100mg test. etc etc
its v person dependant, but an ideal scenario is training 4-5 sessions a week, 20-25 pounds over stage weight, being on a really gd hit of calories. only way to get to that place is training so so hard every session. then u just play with food. and at the end add cardio. that’s an ideal…. but sadly it rarely pans out that way. most people are 30 pounds over and not on all that many calories, so need extra weight sessions and lots of cardio

author: Jordan Peters
content:
It’s no problem, but remember I try to help as much as I can. If people are rude to me , I simply won’t help.
The question regarding your training , train everything across multiple rep ranges, this can be in one session or split heavy / light. In terms of work sets this is person dependent and it depends on your recovery capabilities , if you train a body part twice a week what underpins growth is your ability to recover. So start at maybe 10/12 sets in a session , and vary the rep ranges of those sets and each session vary the exercise selection and then repeat exercises every 3rd session and gauge your progression.
If your progressing lifts easily your training volume is correct , if strength regresses then recovery hasn’t been optimal so either eat more or cut back on work sets to allow for recovery

In this instance ” nobody cares , work harder ” can be put aside buddy
Upgrade your tiger balm to kwang long oil off amazon. And get some single ply elbow sleeves off strength shop. The video we filmed yday for the site shows this exactly as I too have a tricep tendon issue atm.
So how to work around it: pre fatigue on the pec dec, I advise muscle rounds on this , but do them occluded. This is v smart and allows you to fail without stressing the injury .
So I want you to perform 6 sets of 4 reps 10 seconds rest between sets. typically this would be with a weight you do for 15 reps. Then you can normally hit the 24 rep total. This time however due to your injury I want you to use an even lighter weight , so I want you to hold the stretch for 10secondw between each set of 4 reps. So go light as by set 4/5 your pecs will be on fire. This allows you to fail without stressing your injured pec or your elbow tendon.
Now we can get on a machine to press
You can likely just do straight sets now of 12-15 , because your pecs are ruined it shouldn’t hurt the elbow as you will now use a v light load. Here I would do a conventional muscle round , pick a weight you can do for 15 reps and do 6x 4 – 10 seconds rest between sets. You have now hit the pec twice and taken it to failure but used lighter loads so it should be ok.
Tricep work, I would do this actually occluded . I mention this in my blog and il video it again Monday . As I have to do this at present to rid of my tricep tendon pain that’s crept up on me

content:
I like how you have done it v much. What I would suggest is stick to 3 work sets and go for the 10 percent approach . So set one shoot for your heaviest , then lower the load 10 percent or so. And then shoot to match reps or beat reps in set 2 you got in set 1 , then lower weight a further 10 percent from set 2 to 3 and shoot to match reps or beat them for what you got in set 3
Eg
100kg bench for 10
Then 90kh bench for at least ten but the for 11
Then 81kg bench for at least 11 ( if u got 11 in set 2 )
U may need to adjust by 12.5 percent or 15 percent if you as a person doesn’t hold strength well set to set

author: Jordan Peters
content:
Ok after many offseason , many meals force feeding and just finishing an offseason and Prep that saw me force feed worse then ever here is my take
If you can’t do largely whole meals, your body won’t utilise the food as your just overwhelming it with calories. Now I do push this limit and it’s not to say the moment you can’t eat you back off, you want to stay in this uncomfy place with food for a gd few weeks. Here use digestive enzymes with every meal, berberinne and ala with every carb meal. Once then you simply can’t eat any more , it’s time to run a 4-6 week back off phase where you reduce calories initially by 10-15 percent for 2 weeks and see how much you drop. Then reduce by w further 10 percent for a couple weeks then one more reduction again of 5 percent.
So 4000 cals normal diet and hunger dies on you and need liquid meals
Week 1 and 2 3600
Week 3 and 4 3240 hunger should be back here so then shoot for all solid meals
Week 5 and 6 3078 now you will be hungry so add veggies to all solid meals
Then start to creep ur food back up, see if over 4-6 weeks can get it back to maybe 4000 cals with all
Solid food and feeling hungry and utilising the food well. Then from here u can push to 4200/4400 for8-9 weeks before maybe needing only a 3-4 week back off phase before rebuilding
This approach will keep you healthy , hungry, training well, will ensure you stay lean and insulin sensitivity stays high

author: Jordan Peters
content:
So a quick piece of info for you in how I like POwerlifters to make weight. Typically I can pull ten pounds off someone to weigh in , if needed without any detriment to strength.
The few days leading upto a the meet, lower carbs and replace with coconut oil. Just to deplete carbohydrate stores, this serves two purposes, it will lower body weight as fats won’t pull water into the muscle like carbs do ( 2.3g of water per g of carbs) so as the week progresses you can drop 3-4 pounds just from being depleated. Using coconut oil will allow you to have adequate fuel that you don’t feel too tired. I think mentally this is important for a lifter , as if they feel tired days into a meet, it’s hard for them to know that strength is there.
Two days before weigh ins, take water intake up slightly. Then a day prior to weigh ins totally drop sodium. And increase water again. Flushing sodium through will then see you drop water v aggressively through the night off the back of a two day water increase. Cut water off 12 hours before weigh in and once cut , you can use vit c and dandelion. 10g vit c in one hit is pretty strong diuretic.
Once weighed in, is time to fully replenish glycogen stores, the goal is to totally overload them and spill. It’s not bodybuilding so over filing the tank works well. 6 meals of 100g carbs 30g protien for most guys will be adequate. Real bigger guys will need 150.
People with crazy metabolism obv will need more as after a few days lower carbs, you may not properly replenish glycogen in just a day. Using glucose disposal agents will help, 250mg ala , 200mg berberine and 400mcg chronium at each meal will help insulin sensitivty.
Comp day, keeping carbs out from wake to the meet is wise if that’s how precious diet has been set up, as you don’t want to be dumping out serotonin if your not used to it Close to when U lift. So again coconut oil here will suffice as fuel
Cyclic dextrin is pretty much the perfect carb to take in after Your first lift is complete prior to second lift

content:
Back and low volume legs today.
Slight change in focus , more typically hypertrophy based, ensuring I target exactly where I want based on movement analysis , opposed to just ” increase my deadlift” . Although that works v well, it has a point of diminishing returns on cns, joint health, and muscle gains.
So function of lat is extension and adduction of the shoulder. Two best moves to facilitate that are pullovers and Chins . ( can be Pulldowns but Pulldowns can result in a backwards lean, pulling the elbows behind the body isn’t performed by the lat but in that instance lower traps would take over and the movement would be depression of the scapula.
Targeting the middle back which is predominantly comprised of the traps. Function is elevation, depression and retraction of scapula. So movements – face pull variarion, shrug and then a high to low pull.
So today my  session looked:
Chins x 3
Banded pullover x 3 ( keep strength curve constant with bands)
High rep Pulldown x 1 ( to avoid backward lean)
Totally horizontal dumbell row both arms at same time x 2
High pull machine , pulling hard in lower traps x 2
Shrug x 4 ( feeders of 8 reps upto failing weight , I find this ensures I nail contraction)
So what’s left is spinal erectors. And I still need to do extra leg work so …
3 sets of pull throughs x 6
Lying ham 4 x 6 ( feeders again to ensure good contrqctions, so only one real work set)
Leg press 1 x 20
Split now will be
Legs low volume back
Chest bis low volume delts
Rest
Back low volume legs
Delts tris low volume chest
Rest
Repeat
Abs n calves as often as I see fit , every session if feel good.
Counting contractions now, not reps. I want to nail everything through full ranges of motion ( still seeing some idiots lifting in short ranges in my gym, makes no sense at all – ample studies to support full rom being far far superior. Partials have poor stress distribution, results typically in injuries, mainly connective tissue.

author: Jordan Peters
content:
What are your current caloric needs? Work this out by running a food diary for next three days, Jot down EVERYTHING you eat, look on back of food packs and add up calories.
Let’s say your taking in 3500 cals a day. Your protien set at 1.3g/pound. So let’s say you weigh 200 pounds , your protien needs are 260g
Then work out what Calories of fat you have left to eat.
260g of protien x 4 ( protien is 4 cals/g) … 1040 , 3500-1040, devided by 9, leaves U 270g of fat.
So devide evenly over 7 meals , would be 37g protien / 39g of fat per meal.
From here you then drop food, Inceease energy expediture to drop into a cloric deficit

author: Jordan Peters
content:
Hey Matt, dc is indeed Dante trudels invention. I tried to hire Dante 4 years ago to be taught it directly, but he had stopped taking on clients, but luckily Dr scott Stevenson was taking on dantes clients, so I had two years with scott , in which I was taught True dc.
So the principle is low volume, high frequency, which you will hear me talk about a lot. I have always trained body parts as often as I could but was never properly in tune with the volume: frequency balance, which I now feel I am extremely experienced with and why I am able to get the results from clients I do.
The basic approach of dc, is to rest pause sets, so you take a weight you fail on in a certain rep range, and go to failure once you have you take 10-12 deep breaths then go again wtb the Same weight, fail , then repeat a further time. You will only perform a couple of rest pause sets per body part in a session, as they are so v demanding vs a straight set. So you can keep the volume low . Due to volume being low, you can re train that body part again v soon. The more often you train a body part the quicker it will grow.
Please google, Dante cycles for pennies, that article by Dante outlines his original ideas on dc, after reading that, come back here with specific questions and il

Fats pre bed will slow food further and help stabilise blood sugar levels more so. I like nut butters for additional fibre , and I find sleep is improved when using other macros aside from protien alone.

my fraction plates where a god send for me and corinne tonight, i really really advise everyone to get these, here is the link
http://www.savagestrength.co.uk/strength-shop-fractional-plate-set.html
it means u will always always progress with perfect form, sometimes a big jump will totally disrupt form in lifts. so adding 0.25 a side, or even o.o125 a side means perfect form but progress.
perspective…lets say leg sessions are twice a week, one is a squat, so 52 squat sessions a week, adding 0.5kg a week, 26kilos to my squat in a year with no loss of form? il take that all day long thanks 🙂 , as soon as u make a too big a jump on a squat, something in the chain will breakdown, upper back or abs or lower back or glutes…whatever it is, something will halt ur squat, v v small progressions means u keep perfect eccentric control and not tempted to speed up tempo and bounce up reps…. all gyms should have these anyways, but sadly i have only ever been in 1 that does, so we have ours in the gym bag always

254.2 on wake – 2.6 pound drop total
calipers down on sites that mobilise well, held in stubborn sites, v much expected there … stubborn sites will not drop until the body has stopped pulling from easily mobilised sites so there is a huge contrast in my quad/ab/tricep vs my subscap/glute/lower back, waist in half inch which again is v common as guys mobilise visceral fat easier then any other type of fat, i predict another couple weeks of waist dropping in half inch a time, and ab and quad calipers coming down, then my back will start to come in.
ladies, this is the opposite for you, back will come in first, v easy for girls to get their backs peeeeled, but have soft abs and legs.
so dont worry , this is just how we as males and females are generically wired to store/hold/mobilise body fat
changes next week, intra wo carbs halved, so drop to 30g at each now. 65g total carb drop pet day- 260 cal drop, i will up my yohimbine from 15mg to 20mg / day as this aids in stubborn fat mobilisation. my non training day cardio will swap from liss to hiit sprints – as this increases number of mitochondria more so then liss, so the body has greater fat burning potential as its in the mitochondria fat is oxidised, so now just have to mobilise the stubborn fuckers- not an easy task, but back fat feels soft now, so its been broken down a lot and is a reflection of increased blood flow, hard cold fat isnt good!

content:
Matt, digestion is key, so don’t push to the point you can’t stand the site of food/ if you do, don’t stay there long. Mini cut and go again. But go back up slower , if you max our appetite too quick , offseason is done! So it’s slow gradual creeps , spending as long as u can in a surplus before appetite says no more.
Walk a few times a day, 10 min walks control BG really Well, especially post carb meals. After my pwo meal I walk , and after my post post meal I walk. Only for 15 mins or so walking the dog , but it helps a lot.
If you have sleep apnea , get a cpap, you can’t get heavy if you can’t sleep.
If bp is high, lower it with love heart , kidney stack. If it’s still high use ramipril until you can get it under control and then must improve CV health to aid in BP.
Be patient with your drugs, orals will kill most offseasons, so will tren. So you won’t ever see me use those when I’m trying to grow.
Use slightly more whey , then can swap for whole foods when dieting and hungrier .
A good intra shake is key, you can add 50/75/100g carbs to your daily diet and it not be an issue if the carb powder digests perfect , ours was designed for that – with ala , creatine, pharma citrulline to help
Curcumin is a must! It will help every single blood reading , when I’m pushing hard I use 3 caps am and pm !  Again that’s why I made cure coming . It’s my fav version using bcm 95
And then hydration, manage stress, eat your veggies – the little things add up.
Big one, don’t rely on insulin . If I could rewind, it’s the only thing I would never of touched

thread_title: Jordan’s 2019 Log ( NO OFF TOPIC POSTS)
author: Jordan Peters
content:
I will explain a little more , to be helpful , instead of just getting frustrated .
Training is a constant auto regulation , to bring about a novel stimulus. I am a huge believer that low volume, focusing on high intensity is the fastest way to do this, you can train at high frequency, you can get strong very fast and that strength coupled with a surplus builds tons of muscle
As a beginner , training at the highest frequency possible is key, so full body training , once you have built 2 or so years of muscle , an upper lower split is then applicable as body parts need more volume than previous. However volume is still low , and therefore intensity is still high. Again let’s nail a couple years here, and we get to push pull leg variations volume per body part increases but volume is still low ish. At this point driving strength is still absolutely key , accumulating volume really isn’t necessary just for the sake of it, you will just hinder your ability to get crazy strong .
Again fast forward a period of time and body parts need to be split up again, more volume again. At this point it becomes harder to keep gaining strength and then focusing on total work through accumulating volume is a more logical option, rir is the most logical way to accumulate maximal work.
Through this process, volume goes up and down depending on recovery , intensity goes up and down depending on recovery : extending sets with PR is a great tool , if recovery Permits.
I really hope posts like this show the bigger picture that there isn’t a system, or a method , but just logical alterations within someone’s needs and recovery capabilities . Page 94 🙂

content:
Great Ireland trip! Thanks to everyone that came .
My only critique of the whole trip…. fuck Dublin airport! / aer lingus. Man that is some seriously poor organisation there, an hour to check in, and then another 30 mins to get through security , simply because it was so poorly organised. Anyways , that aside haha, amazing trip .

@corinne
and I had a great push session.
I can honestly say this prep has been the biggest test for Corinne , not physically as she is capable physically of anything , but mentally in that her offseason ending point was truly perfect ; she over came her demons and pushed her body weight upto a lean 175 , 30 pounds over stage weight ! She look unreal! And then this prep has been a total prick, in that right now she should be inside out , but still, she isn’t , and it’s just been a real kick in the teeth , at the idea of , how work and consistency prevails. In the end it does, but she is being tested for sure right now, and it almost feels unfair , in that she should be where she wants to be, but she isn’t . Alas, we don’t moan, and man we don’t do pity ,  but just a reminder to ourselves and everyone that you will be tested , and tested , and it’s how you deal with those tests, do you crumble or do you keep pushing and have faith that your ability to work hard will always pull you through . I have that faith for sure .
I’m into my 5th week cruising , feel happy and fit , and generally excited to tidy up a bit and kick back up drugs when needed

So this is how you may programme across the week :
Session 1
2 ham curl
3 leg press

Session 2 ( 4 days later maybe. )
2 ham curl

thread_title: Jordan’s 2019 Log ( NO OFF TOPIC POSTS)
author: Jordan Peters
content:
Luke, never at the same time , but I have tried diff drugs at diff doses to see their effectiveness vs sides
For me, 1400 primo is amazing ! No sides , great strength , no water, appetite issues .
I have run test at 2000mg , Hated it. Did absolutely no better than 1000mg just with way more water and sides. I found 750mg to be my most effective dose.
Nandrolone have ran at 1500mg , awful dose, felt like shit . For me best dose is 500/600mg
Eq I have run at 1750, crippling anxiety , best dose for me was 900mg.
Tren I have run at 1050mg , this was just overkill , for me 700 is just spot on.
Mast have run at 1000, does no more than 700.
Winnie at 100 doesn’t give more than Winnie at 50 / day
Halo at 50 works superbly well combined with Winny
My test levels atm are reflective of 900ish mg , which feels gd for me atm tbh. So next offseason I would defo come out of a cruise and look to build up to 750-1000 test , if I could handle it ok. And nandrolone start at 300 and work to 600. At some point use an oral it get stuck at plateaus strength wise
I have run every drug possible really , enough to know that you can build a crazy amount of muscle on 500-600mg test and 200mg of nandrolone and gd food. And when things get stuck, creep up the dose

author: Jordan Peters
content:
Drew, spend some time reading my posts a bit my man. I’m guessing you haven’t watched any of my videos in the beginners section or videos on training volume? 🙂
In short, I am absolutely a low volume advocate. ( you can see this from my sessions, I did 2 sets compound chest work, 2 sets iso work, done! ) I am in favour of higher frequency training. It makes No sense to train at low volume and low frequency – literally that is illogical. Low volume means you can expose the muscle to the stimulus sooner as you have caused less damage. Extending recovery days beyond what you need, just means less chances to expose that muscle to a stimulus across a 6/12 month period. Think 52vs 104 chances to grow a year.

thread_title: Partials on an exercise, whats the benefits?
author: Jordan Peters
content: Our body will use the fibres it needs to get the job done , failing with partials , means we are grabbing onto every last ounce of fibre we have and exhausting it – not always necessary , but on some exercises it’s a v effective tool

thread_title: Going 'cold turkey' on cardio after prep.
author: Jordan Peters
content: Controlling your rebound will be if u binge or not . The 200-400 cals u expend cutting out the cardio won’t make the smallest diff post show . I personally stop any at all, but then also I don’t binge post show , so I don’t rebound .

author: Jordan Peters
content: You don’t necessarily NEED anything , aside from maybe creatine , high quality omega 3 , evening primrose oil, a good whey ( for convenience ) , maybe a good greens powder . These things don’t change between lean bulk/ diet phase . All that changes is your caloric intake .

thread_title: Cardio or Reducing Caloric Intake to increase deficit?
author: Jordan Peters
content: Cardio WILL work, but this is v person dependent , I favour lowering cals , others like Corinne and James prefer to move a little more . Both create a deficit , it comes down to which tool serves you best , so … time to learn your body a bit 🙂 , add some cardio , see what happens , next move lower some cals, see what happens ….

content:
Until you are big , you must must must drive the scale up. However u get there, eat and eat and eat . Push them up until your at a body fat limit ( don’t ask what this is, totally depends on the person) diet down and then go again and beat the last scale weight and beat all ur lifts. I started at 158 pounds onstage my first show 10 years ago. I ate and ate , force fed until I was sick , over and over , until I got the size I wanted . Most people just don’t have the bollocks for it, it’s hard, that’s why you don’t see many people hit 300 pounds at my height . Simply comes down to your goals and if you want to reach them, or just like the idea of reaching them but never really get stuck into them.

thread_title: Jordan’s 2018 Log ( NO OFF TOPIC POSTS)
author: Jordan Peters
content:
Hey buddy , this prep I feel leaving tools in the tank is more important than ever  🙂 . Rebound phase imo post show needs to be less drugs and doing the v best you can on less when food is high . So let’s say for most of the offseason you never go over 1g of drugs, it could be 500mg test , 300npp , 200 eq. Or whatever it is, that has you look/feel great and able to eat your food. For me it would be maybe 300 test , 400-500primo ( or dhb) and then 200npp ( or maybe trestalone ) .
Then prep starts and u take ur cals down and ur first move is bump test or trestalone a little to help fullness. Through that early / middle phase of prep I think you could recomp like crazy , as drugs go to 1100-1200-1300mg / week , looking to drop fat well but really stay full and strong. Then we still have tren to play with at the later end of prep when strength and fullness dips, maybe adding a bit more test / trest , and then tren at 175mg/week to start.
So now we are on say:
300test
450dhb/primo
400 trestalone ( or more test + some eq)
175 tren
Total drugs are still super low here , but fullness and strength would be an absolute peak !
Then it would be 50mg mast p ed , and tren to 50mg ed
Totals now :
300 test
450 dhb/primo
400 trestalone
350 tren
350 mast
1850 total
Last 3 weeks : 50mg anavar + Winnie + halo /
Day
That imo would be the perfect use of all your tools 🙂

Jaglio , great question 🙂 . I think your spot on people feel they NEED to change . I don’t want to change ever once I’m on a run of stuff feeling gd, I will eeek out every drop of progress I can possible. Right now also I have no forced reps and I don’t attempt reps I can’t complete. When I’m in a cal surplus I may do this more so .
For me my auto regulation is based most on fitness , so I don’t apply to most ppl. Offseason for me is harder to work at max capacity – liss doesn’t fix this, just makes my legs small. Hiit would fix it, but programming it in is hard when recovery is on the limit . So for me I need to weigh up if being heavy is worth it or can I make more gains stopping at maybe 270 and tidying back upto 250
And going back upto 270 , repeating that mini cut process each time eeking out 2 pounds here and there of muscle .
Another example this week was sat , my second Ham curl move , 3rd set totally bombed , next time will just do 2 sets , I know the 3rd isn’t constructive here . So this autoregulation of volume while in a deficit can be provided by feedback from your log book

thread_title: Jordan’s 2018 Log ( NO OFF TOPIC POSTS)
author: Jordan Peters
content:
🙂 no problem . So I will answer a diff question , why am I doing that….
Atm I want my sessions to burn as many cals as possible , I don’t use cardio as a fat loss tool, my legs just shrink. Last year I took steps to 10k a legs shrunk , the year
Before the same. This year kept my steps to a mimimum and my legs are still around 29.5 inches , filled up they would be 30s and they are super lean now. So let’s focus on another question : at what point should cardio be used as a tool? So I have coached HUNDREDS of people and there is huge variation in who can handle liss, hiit and then training how I train. So we need a caloric deficit to Achieve fat loss , I think for some , you can take cals as low as they need to go, be it even 7-8 cals per pound bodyweight , which is ultra low , but if they are rested enough to train hard they will get in shape without losing any muscle. Then you will have some people that at 10 cals per pound will do better with more food and then dropping into a deficit by adding cardio. There is NO fixed number at which then cardio is a requirement , it’s a totally person dependent thing.
Corinne has her steps go to circa 15,000 in a prep and loses no muscle at all in her legs. So what you have to work out is, how do I keep all my muscle  from offseason while getting shredded , without losing any body parts. To me , it’s the worst look in the world when legs have whittled away to nothing , that’s why I dropped prep last year as my legs went down to 27.5 inches, they literally died on me. I’m not putting that crap onstage , even if they would be bigger than others, mine are 29+ legs that have worked so hard for.
So atm, my sessions are 2.5-3 hours long , and I use 5-6 sets of 12-20 rep of leg compound moves, 2 Times a week for quads .
Then same again for hams . To absolutely ramp cal expenditure . Now if I still had to do more… which I dont , but Corinne likely will when she preps as she got a bit too fat , that session may need to split am /pm , gives scope for more volume again , and at the end of the quad session , can add hiit but something very heavy , like heavy prowler work. So basically more leg work 🙂
I hope that answers the questions that some of you may have 🙂

author: Jordan Peters
content:
My usual advise for rehab, if there is any pain at all, even the smallest amount. Don’t do it
Gradually build load/volume until your back to normal. This may take 3 months or may take 6 , to at a rate that ensures you avoid pain

author: Jordan Peters
content:
Volume imo should always decrease
Let’s look at volume like this: we do the max volume we can recover from to grow when in hypertrophy phases
The max we can recover from is usually a fair bit higher what we can do as a minimum to maintain muscle
So lower volume to the minimum work we can do to maintain for a week
So let’s say for back you do 15-20
Sets a week total for max hypertrophy. You could cut that in half for the week and maintain , while u let ur body recover.
Just an adjustment in volume alone will allow recovery . Now if you leave a rep in the tank too and don’t fail. Recovery will be hugely improved further

thread_title: Jordan’s 2018 Log ( NO OFF TOPIC POSTS)
author: Jordan Peters
content: So For those that struggle with consistency, you just have to ask yourself what makes you happy. If you like to eat junk / go out and that makes you happy then keep doing that, I’m not going to say you should change . But if you want a diff path , then obv it comes down to the idea that will that alternative path make you happier . If your absolutely fucking miserable while dieting , then that isn’t living imo . Only one life , don’t spend it being miserable, but if you can make gradual changes to your lifestyle so have best of both , then that’s perfect . I think ppl often set themselves unrealistic levels of adherence. If you struggle to be consistent then plan in periods that help you with this, so X amount of off plan meals a a week. That will still see huge progress vs no plan at all

author: Jordan Peters
content:
All of those questions are loaded.
Caloric deficit – what causes fat loss. How you achieve this is totally person dependant . Does cardio hinder recover , does high intensity cardio hinder recovery. Does low food impact adherence .
The questions above will make it tailored to you.
So only you can decide which route to take to drop into a caloric deficit.
Rate of fat loss – again loaded question. Can you drop more without losing performance in the gym . You tell me? Do it and find out. Then you will learn for next time.
Hopefully this has made you think about your options. Instead of someone just saying ,
Do hiit cardio. Which would just be dog shit advise
